## Paper

Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Independent versus Cooperative Agents

## World

cross_world_methods

## Institution

Not applicable: method paper.

## Agent type

Independent multi-agent Q-learning / independent DQN learners.

## Theoretical benchmark

MARL baseline benchmark: each agent learns its own policy while treating other learners as part of the environment.

## Learning setup

Separate learner per agent, separate exploration and replay streams, no shared parameters, and shared environment feedback only through interaction.

## Metrics

Behavioral divergence from single-agent/shared baselines, coordination outcomes, welfare/exploitability/stability, and tests for seed/replay independence.

## Main result

Independent learners can outperform cooperative agents in certain scenarios, but cooperation can lead to faster learning at the cost of communication; sharing sensation, episodes, or learned policies can be beneficial if used efficiently

## What they prove

If n reinforcement-learning agents who can observe everything about each other can decrease the required learning time at a rate that is Θ(1/n)

## What they only simulate

The performance of n independent agents with the one of n cooperative agents and to identify their tradeoffs

## What they do NOT test

The practical study of comparing the performance of n independent agents with the one of n cooperative agents

## What we need to reproduce

Reproduce independent learning as a genuine MARL condition: no shared network, no shared replay buffer, no shared exploration stream, and no aliasing with plain DQN. Evidence must come from minds/marl/independent_learners.py; decorrelation tests; fixed independent-DQN full outputs..

## How our project differs

The paper contrasts independent and cooperative multi-agent learning. This repo uses independent-DQN as a capability-ladder condition and must show it is not just DQN duplicated under the same random stream.

## Implementation obligations

Per-agent learner objects; decorrelated SeedSequence child streams; per-agent replay buffers; per-agent epsilon-greedy RNGs; separate network initialization; tests that Q-values/rollouts diverge under one base seed.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

minds/marl/independent_learners.py; decorrelation tests; fixed independent-DQN full outputs in Pricing Arena and Resource Island; cross-world ladder comparison tables.

## Failure modes to audit

Subclass alias of DQN; seed + index streams that still collapse under symmetry; shared replay/global np.random/random/torch state; reporting independent-DQN rows that are bit-identical to DQN.
